name: pci_set_powerstate_method
prose: Precondition: child is a PCI device whose ivars hold a valid pci_devinfo. Postcondition: returns EOPNOTSUPP, before any config read or write, if the device has no power management capability (pp_location == 0); returns 0 without a config write or delay if the current power state from pci_get_powerstate equals state; otherwise it reads the power status register (a config read that happens before the state is validated), then returns EOPNOTSUPP without writing if state is D1 or D2 and the matching D1SUPP or D2SUPP capability bit is clear, or EINVAL without writing if state is not one of D0, D1, D2, D3; for a supported state it optionally prints a message when bootverbose, writes the power status register with the old non-state bits kept and the new state bits set, busy-waits 10000 us when the higher of the old and new states is D3, 200 us when it is D2, none otherwise, and returns 0.
note: pci.c:2874-2945. Reviewer 2 right: PCI_READ_CONFIG at 2912 runs before the D1/D2 EOPNOTSUPP (2920,2925) and EINVAL (2932) returns, so 'without touching hardware' was wrong (reads, not writes). Early returns 2882 (EOPNOTSUPP), 2891 (0), 2920/2925 (EOPNOTSUPP), 2932 (EINVAL), 2944 (0).

name: pci_dw_init
prose: Precondition: dev is a DesignWare PCI host-bridge device; the glue driver is expected to have set sc->dbi_res before the call (this function does not allocate it). Postcondition: sets sc->dev and sc->node, initializes sc->mtx, sets bus_start 0, bus_end 255, root_bus 0, sub_bus 1, reads coherent and num-lanes from the OFW node (num_lanes defaults to 1), then returns 0 if every step succeeds. Steps and failures: num_lanes not 1, 2, 4 or 8 sets num_lanes to 0 and returns ENXIO; missing 'config' in reg-names returns ENXIO; failure to allocate the config memory resource returns ENXIO; bus_dma_tag_create, ofw_pcib_init, pci_dw_decode_ranges, pci_dw_detect_out_atu_regions and pci_dw_setup_hw return their nonzero error unchanged. If pci_dw_detect_atu_unroll reports unroll mode, the 'atu' entry in reg-names is looked up: found means the resource is allocated (ENXIO if NULL) with offset 0; ENOENT means iatu_ur_res aliases dbi_res with the default DBI offset and size; any other lookup error returns ENXIO. On success it calls device_add_child for 'pci', whose result is ignored, and returns 0. Every error goes to label out, which returns rv with no cleanup (XXX Cleanup), so the mutex, resources and dma tag already created are left in place.

Returns: gotos at 733,741,749,771,775,779,796,807,813,821 all to out:826 -> return rv (828); success return 0 at 825. name: pcib_pcie_hotplug_task
prose: Precondition: used as a taskqueue handler with context pointing to the pcib_softc; the caller does not hold the hotplug lock. Postcondition: takes PCIB_HP_LOCK, then calls pcib_hotplug_present(sc). If it returns nonzero and sc->child is NULL, it sets sc->child to the result of device_add_child(dev, 'pci', DEVICE_UNIT_ANY) (which may be NULL on failure) and calls bus_attach_children(dev); if it returns nonzero and sc->child is already set, nothing changes. If it returns zero and sc->child is non-NULL, it calls device_delete_child and clears sc->child only when that returns 0; if it returns zero and sc->child is NULL, nothing changes. It then releases the lock and returns nothing (void). The pending argument is unused.

name: pci_ioctl
prose: Precondition: dev, data and td are valid for cmd, with data pointing at the command-specific structure, and the caller does not hold the bus topology lock. Behavior: if flag lacks FWRITE and cmd is not one of PCIOCGETCONF (and its 32-bit, FreeBSD14 and FreeBSD6 compat variants when compiled), PCIOCGETBAR or PCIOCLISTVPD, it returns EPERM before taking any lock; so PCIOCREAD, PCIOCWRITE, PCIOCATTACHED, PCIOCBARMMAP, PCIOCBARIO and unknown commands get EPERM on a read-only descriptor. Otherwise it takes the bus topology lock, dispatches on cmd, each case ends in break, then releases the lock and returns error. Results: PCIOCGETCONF initializes error to 0 and returns 0 for the list-changed and past-the-end cases with a status code, EINVAL when pattern sizes are inconsistent, when only one of num_patterns or pat_buf_len is nonzero, or when copyin of the patterns fails, the copyout error if copying a match out fails, otherwise 0; it frees its temporary buffers. PCIOCREAD and PCIOCWRITE (and the FreeBSD6 forms) return EINVAL for a width other than 1, 2 or 4 or for a negative or misaligned register, ENODEV when the device is not found (except FreeBSD6 read with COMPAT_FREEBSD4, which stores -1 and returns 0), else 0 after the config read or write. PCIOCGETBAR returns ENODEV, EINVAL (no such BAR) or 0. PCIOCATTACHED returns ENODEV or 0. PCIOCLISTVPD returns ENODEV or the result of pci_list_vpd. PCIOCBARMMAP returns ENODEV or the result of pci_bar_mmap (the inner EPERM check for read-write mapping without FWRITE is unreachable on a read-only descriptor because it is rejected earlier). PCIOCBARIO returns ENODEV or the pci_bar_io result. Any other command returns ENOTTY.
note: pci_user.c:1112-1579. Reviewer round 17 mixed: right that GETBAR/LISTVPD/GETCONF are allowed read-only; but PCIOCBARMMAP/PCIOCBARIO are NOT in the read-only list (1143-1161) so they get EPERM at 1163 without FWRITE; the reviewer's 'proceed without FWRITE' is wrong. Round 15 reviewer about BARMMAP EPERM only with RW flag (1547-1549): reachable only with FWRITE clear, which is already rejected at 1141, so unreachable. Name 'pci_ioctl' is at 1112, in the real file (slice name complaint was spurious). Not verified: bodies of pci_list_vpd/pci_bar_mmap/pci_bar_io.

name: tdsaConfigRoutingInfoRespRcvd
prose: Handles the response to an SMP CONFIGURE ROUTE INFORMATION request for an expander device; returns void. Precondition: oneDeviceData has a port context and a tdExpander; frameHeader holds the SMP response header. If onePortContext->valid is agFALSE it calls tdsaSASDiscoverAbort and returns. If frameHeader->smpFunctionResult is neither SMP_FUNCTION_ACCEPTED nor PHY_VACANT it calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiRoot, onePortContext, tiError). Otherwise it takes DownStreamExpander = oneExpander->tdCurrentDownStreamExpander; if that is non-NULL it increments its currentUpStreamPhyIndex; it increments oneExpander->currentDownStreamPhyIndex; then only if DownStreamExpander is non-NULL: if its currentUpStreamPhyIndex is below numOfUpStreamPhys it adds a routing entry (tdsaSASRoutingEntryAdd) for that upstream phy with oneExpander's configSASAddressHi/Lo, with no condition on oneExpander->tdUpStreamExpander; otherwise it looks up the upstream expander and a configurable expander and, if the upstream expander is non-NULL, checks for a duplicate configured SAS address: when a configurable expander exists and the address is not a duplicate it sets UpStreamExpander->tdCurrentDownStreamExpander to oneExpander, updates the configurable expander's currentDownStreamPhyIndex and sets its tdReturnginExpander to oneExpander->tdReturnginExpander, resets DownStreamExpander->currentUpStreamPhyIndex to 0 and adds a routing entry on the configurable expander's current downstream phy; otherwise it takes ReturningExpander = oneExpander->tdReturnginExpander, resets DownStreamExpander->currentUpStreamPhyIndex to 0 and, if ReturningExpander is non-NULL, sets discovery.status to DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM and, when the returning expander's discoveringPhyId is below its device's numOfPhys, calls tdsaDiscoverSend if its discoverSMPAllowed is agTRUE (then clearing it), else (all phys done) sets discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE, removes it from the discovering list and calls tdsaSASDownStreamDiscovering. When DownStreamExpander or the upstream expander is NULL the corresponding branch does nothing (apart from the increments above). It then returns.

Reviewer 1 right (no-op paths when DownStreamExpander or UpStreamExpander NULL, 5392, 5415, 5497); reviewer 2 right (first routing entry branch 5394-5406 does not test oneExpander->tdUpStreamExpander); old prose also wrongly said the configurable-expander branch re-points the configurable expander's tdReturnginExpander at oneExpander (5435 assigns oneExpander->tdReturnginExpander). name: tdsaSMPBusyTimerCB
prose: Timer callback that retries an SMP request after a busy indication; returns void. timerData1, timerData2 and timerData3 are the port context, the device data and the SMP request body. It starts with status = AGSA_RC_FAILURE, increments discovery->SMPRetries, and only if SMPRetries is still below SMP_BUSY_RETRIES calls saSMPStart for the request on tdsaAllShared->SMPQNum with ossaSMPCompleted as completion. Then: if status is AGSA_RC_SUCCESS it resets SMPRetries to 0 and kills discovery->SMPBusyTimer if running (discovery is not completed here); if status is AGSA_RC_FAILURE (including the case where no call was made because the retry limit was reached) it resets SMPRetries to 0, calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiRoot, onePortContext, tiError) and kills the busy timer if running; otherwise (AGSA_RC_BUSY from the call) it either, when SMPRetries is >= SMP_BUSY_RETRIES, resets SMPRetries, calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) and kills the busy timer, or re-arms the busy timer through tdsaSMPBusyTimer. It returns nothing.
note: itddisc.c:8024-8115 (packet name had this as tdsaSMPBusyTimerCB with slice 7908-8158 starting in tdsaSMPBusyTimer's area). Reviewer 1 right (success only resets retries and kills the timer, 8069-8078); reviewer 2 right (initial status is FAILURE so no call made means failure path with discovery done, 8041, 8080-8090; busy with retries exhausted ends discovery 8094-8105). The busy-exhausted branch can only be reached after a call was made with retries below the limit, so in practice it does not trigger, but the code has it.

name: ossaSATAEvent
prose: SATA event callback of the TISA initiator layer; defined only when FDS_SM is not defined (#ifndef FDS_SM at 10986). Returns void. Precondition for the NCQ path: agDevHandle and its osData point to valid device data (not checked). On OSSA_IO_XFER_ERROR_ABORTED_NCQ_MODE: if the device's satDriveState is SAT_DEV_STATE_NORMAL it sets it to SAT_DEV_STATE_IN_RECOVERY and allocates an internal IO resource for READ LOG EXT page 10h; if the allocation returns NULL it sets satAbortAfterReset to agTRUE and returns (the device reset is inside #ifdef NOT_YET and not compiled); otherwise it prepares the internal IO context and calls satSendReadLogExt; if that does not return tiSuccess it frees the internal IO resource, sets satAbortAfterReset to agTRUE and returns; on success the recovery continues in the READ LOG EXT completion. If the drive is not in the NORMAL state it only logs. For the other listed events (command frame issued, PIO setup error, IT-nexus-loss variants, DEK key tag mismatch, DIF mismatch with a frame read that returns early on a NULL agParam or too-short length) it only logs or reads the DIF details. For any other event it takes the request body from agIORequest->osData and, if the event is OSSA_IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_STP_RESOURCES_BUSY and tdsaAllShared->FCA is set, sends one SMP hard reset through tdsaPhyControlSend when NumOfFCA is not positive (incrementing it), else, when the device is registered and ResetInDiscovery is 0, aborts all IO on it (tdsaAbortAll), marks it invalid, not registered, and reports a device-removal event with ostiInitiatorEvent.

Reviewer 1 right (guard satDriveState==NORMAL at 11091, recovery-in-progress only logs 11194); reviewer 2 right (allocation failure only sets satAbortAfterReset 11114, reset inside #ifdef NOT_YET 11117). Returns 11129, 11191, 11242, 11247. Old prose omitted the generic else branch at 11265-11313. PARTLY READ: lines 11194-11265 (logging-only events) seen via control-flow lines.

name: satWriteSame10CB
prose: Completion callback of the ATA command used to emulate SCSI WRITE SAME(10) in pieces; returns void. It locates the original request: if satIntIo is NULL the request itself is the original; otherwise the original context comes from satIOContext->satOrgIOContext, and if that is NULL the function returns immediately, before marking the request body completed. It then sets tdIORequestBody->ioCompleted to agTRUE and ioStarted to agFALSE. If agFirstDword is NULL and agIOStatus is not OSSA_IO_SUCCESS it sets NO_SENSE/no-additional-info sense, completes the original with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION through ostiInitiatorIOCompleted, decrements pending IO, frees the internal IO resource and returns. If agIOStatus is not success and the FIS type is not REG_DEV_TO_HOST or SET_DEV_BITS, or the ATA status has the ERR or DF bit set: an OSSA_IO_ABORTED status goes through satProcessAbort (the original is not completed by this function), otherwise the original is completed with CHECK_CONDITION and NO_SENSE sense; in both cases it then decrements pending IO, frees the internal IO resource and returns (the command-specific switch at 6197 only logs). Otherwise (success) it decrements pending IO and frees the internal IO resource, takes the LBA and transfer length from the original CDB, computes the sector count (a zero transfer length means up to 0x0FFFFFFF-1 minus lba), and, depending on how many sectors satSectorDone already covers, completes the original or allocates a new internal IO and issues the next satWriteSame10_1 for the next LBA range, completing the original with an error and returning if the allocation or issue fails.

Reviewer 1 right (abort goes through satProcessAbort 6180-6186); reviewer 2 right (the NULL-satOrgIOContext return at 6081-6084 precedes the ioCompleted/ioStarted marking at 6098-6099). PARTLY READ: success-path completion/next-piece logic 6297-6469 via control-flow lines only (which status the original is completed with in each sub-branch not verified).

name: satLogSense
prose: SAT translation of SCSI LOG SENSE; returns tiSuccess (when it completes the request itself) or the status of the lower call it delegates to. With NACA or LINK set in cdb[9] it sets ILLEGAL REQUEST / INVALID FIELD IN CDB, completes with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION and returns tiSuccess. AllocLen is computed as (bit8)((cdb[7] << 8) + cdb[8]), so only the low 8 bits of the allocation length are kept. When AllocLen is 4 it writes only a 4-byte page header into the caller's buffer for the supported-pages page (length 1, 2 or 3 depending on SMART support), the self-test-results page (length 0x190) or the information-exceptions page, without checking SMART support, and completes with SCSI_STAT_GOOD; any other page code completes with CHECK_CONDITION / INVALID FIELD IN CDB. For other allocation lengths: the supported-pages page writes the header and list (0x00, plus 0x10 when SMART is supported, plus 0x2F when SMART self-test is supported), copies MIN(AllocLen, list size) bytes, and completes with tiIOUnderRun and residual AllocLen - lenRead when AllocLen is larger, otherwise with SCSI_STAT_GOOD; the self-test-results page completes with CHECK_CONDITION / INVALID FIELD IN CDB when SMART self-test is not supported, otherwise returns satLogSenseAllocate's status (LOG_SENSE_0 when SMART is not enabled, with 512 bytes LOG_SENSE_1 when 48-bit addressing is supported, else LOG_SENSE_2); the information-exceptions page completes with INVALID FIELD IN CDB when the SMART feature set is absent, with ABORTED COMMAND / ATA DEVICE FEATURE NOT ENABLED when SMART is not enabled, and otherwise builds a SMART RETURN STATUS FIS, sets satCompleteCB to satLogSenseCB and returns sataLLIOStart's status; an unknown page code completes with CHECK_CONDITION / INVALID FIELD IN CDB. After the switch (for the paths that completed inline) it returns tiSuccess.
note: sat.c:11594-11997 (slice 11658-11925). Reviewer 1 right (tiIOUnderRun at 11809-11814 and delegated satLogSenseAllocate returns at 11860, 11878, 11892); reviewer 2 right (AllocLen==4 path writes header-only pages for self-test and information-exceptions without testing SMART support, 11700-11719, and the supported-pages page then carries no list, 11675-11698). Old prose wrongly described rejection of those pages at AllocLen 4. Not read: satLogSenseAllocate and satLogSenseCB bodies.

name: satSendDiagnostic
prose: SAT translation of SCSI SEND DIAGNOSTIC; returns tiSuccess when it completes inline or the status of sataLLIOStart when it submits an ATA FIS. At entry it sets pSatDevData->satVerifyState to 0 and satBGPendingDiag to agFALSE. It completes with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION and ILLEGAL REQUEST / INVALID FIELD IN CDB (returning tiSuccess) when the PF, DEVOFFL or UNITOFFL bit is set or the parameter list length bytes cdb[3] and cdb[4] are not both 0, when NACA or LINK is set in cdb[5], or when the self-test bit is clear and SMART self-test is not supported; it completes with CHECK_CONDITION and ABORTED COMMAND / ATA DEVICE FEATURE NOT ENABLED when the self-test bit is clear, SMART self-test is supported and SMART is not enabled. When the self-test bit is set and SMART self-test is unsupported, or supported but SMART not enabled, it builds a non-data READ VERIFY SECTORS (EXT form when 48-bit addressing is supported) FIS for one sector at LBA 0 and returns sataLLIOStart's status. When the self-test bit is set and SMART self-test and SMART are both enabled it builds a SMART EXECUTE OFF-LINE IMMEDIATE FIS and returns sataLLIOStart's status. When the self-test bit is clear and both SMART self-test and SMART are enabled it switches on the self-test code (cdb[1] bits >> 5): codes 1 and 2 set satBGPendingDiag to agTRUE, first complete the request with SCSI_STAT_GOOD through ostiInitiatorIOCompleted and then build and submit a SMART EXECUTE OFF-LINE IMMEDIATE FIS; code 4 completes with CHECK_CONDITION if the parameter length is nonzero or if no background test is pending, otherwise submits the FIS; codes 5 and 6 build and submit an FIS; other codes (0, 3, 7, default) fall out and complete with SCSI_STAT_GOOD, returning tiSuccess. The satCompleteCB for submitted FISes is satSendDiagnosticCB.

Reviewer 1 right (background self-test codes 1 and 2 complete GOOD inline then submit the FIS, 9272-9319, 9321-9369); reviewer 2 right (satBGPendingDiag is cleared at entry 9016 but set to agTRUE at 9272 and 9321). Not read: FIS contents for codes 5/6 beyond control flow (9459-9538); SMART self-test code semantics not verified.

name: dmUpStreamDiscover2ExpanderPhy
prose: Handles one SAS2 DISCOVER response for the phy oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during upstream discovery; returns void. Precondition: dmRoot, onePortContext, oneExpander (with oneExpander->dmDevice set) and pDiscoverResp are valid. Behavior: if dmDiscoverCheck returns agTRUE it returns at once with no change. If pDiscoverResp->phyIdentifier differs from oneExpander->discoveringPhyId it calls dmDiscoverDone(dmRoot, onePortContext, DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns, without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError and without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Otherwise it stores the response's routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId]. If the expander's device is a fanout expander and the routing attribute is subtractive, it records the device's SAS address and the phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns; a fanout expander with any other routing attribute does nothing further in this step. For a non-fanout expander with an attached device and subtractive routing: it calls dmExpanderUpStreamPhyAdd. If hasUpStreamDevice was already set, an upstream SAS address that differs from the attached address while the attached device is an edge or fanout expander makes it record the error address and call dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) without returning. If hasUpStreamDevice was not set, it sets it and the upstream SAS address; when the attached address is not the port's local address it looks the attached device up with dmPortSASDeviceFind: if found and an edge expander, it either links oneExpander->dmUpStreamExpander to that expander when its upstream address matches this device, or else records the error address and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE); if found and not an edge expander, it only logs a debug message and calls neither dmDiscoverDone nor records an error; if not found it adds the device with dmPortSASDeviceAdd (STP type for STP target or SATA, otherwise SAS type, link rate the minimum of the port's rate and the reported one; in non-full-start discovery first trying dmFindRegNValid), and if the add produced a device it allocates and registers an expander for an attached edge or fanout expander (setting oneExpander->dmUpStreamExpander) or, for an end device, sets that device's dmExpander to oneExpander and clears dmUpStreamExpander; a failed device add or a failed expander allocation calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError. Every path that did not return early then increments oneExpander->discoveringPhyId; if the discovery status is still DISCOVERY_UP_STREAM it either calls dmDiscoverSend (more phys remain) or dmUpdateAllAdjacent, dmDiscoveringExpanderRemove and dmUpStreamDiscovering; otherwise it just returns.
note: dmdisc.c:1008-1416 (slice 1088-1388 is the middle). Returns at 1030, 1075, 1101, 1415. Reviewer round 15 right (add failure 1377 and alloc failure 1362 do not record sasAddressIDDiscoverError); original reviewer right (non-edge branch 1210-1214 only logs). Old prose wrongly said add/alloc failures record the error. Callee bodies (dmPortSASDeviceAdd, dmFindRegNValid, dmDiscoverDone) not read; only their call sites.

name: dmDownStreamDiscoverExpanderPhy
prose: Handles one SAS 1.1 DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during downstream discovery; returns void. Behavior: returns at once with no change if dmDiscoverCheck returns agTRUE. If pDiscoverResp->phyIdentifier differs from discoveringPhyId it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError and without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Otherwise it stores the response's routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId] and sets oneExpander->discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE. When the response reports an attached device: direct routing to an attached edge or fanout expander records the expander's SAS address and the phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Otherwise, if the attached SAS address differs from the port's local address it looks up the device with dmPortSASDeviceFind. If not found and the routing is subtractive with an attached edge or fanout expander, it records the error address and sets onePortContext->discovery.DeferredError to agTRUE without calling dmDiscoverDone; if not found otherwise it adds the device with dmPortSASDeviceAdd (STP type for STP target or SATA, otherwise SAS type, at the minimum of the port link rate and the reported rate; in non-full-start discovery it first tries dmFindRegNValid) and sets its dmExpander to oneExpander; for table routing with an attached fanout expander it records the error and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE), with an attached edge expander it allocates an expander, adds the up and down phys and queues it, or calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) if allocation fails. If the device was already known, the checks on subtractive and table routing can record the error and call dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) without returning. No attached device, or an attached address equal to the local address, adds nothing. Each path that did not return early then increments discoveringPhyId; if the status is still DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM it either calls dmDiscoverSend (discoveringPhyId < numOfPhys) or dmUpdateAllAdjacent, dmDiscoveringExpanderRemove and dmDownStreamDiscovering; otherwise it returns.

Reviewer 1 mixed: right that subtractive error to a new expander sets DeferredError (1588) not termination; reviewer 2 right that mismatch records no sasAddressIDDiscoverError (1485-1491). PARTLY READ: lines 1690-2118 were read only through control-flow lines (error records + dmDiscoverDone at 1742,1856,1877,1899,1936,1965, no return); dmFindConfigurableExp / routing-entry configuration, UndoAdd and SAS2SAS11 detail not described.

name: dmDownStreamDiscoverExpanderPhy
prose: Handles one SAS 1.1 DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during downstream discovery; returns void. Behavior: returns at once with no change if dmDiscoverCheck returns agTRUE. If the response's phy id differs from discoveringPhyId it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError and without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Otherwise it stores the routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId] and sets discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE. With an attached device, direct routing to an edge or fanout expander records the error address and phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Other cases add or look up the attached device (dmPortSASDeviceFind, dmPortSASDeviceAdd, dmFindRegNValid), allocate and queue an attached edge expander, or on topology errors (subtractive routing with no recorded upstream device or an upstream address mismatch, table routing to a fanout expander, and similar) record the error address and call dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) without returning; a subtractive-routed unknown expander instead sets DeferredError to agTRUE. After those, the paths that did not return early reach the increment of discoveringPhyId (line 2119) and check the status: if it is still DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM it calls dmDiscoverSend when discoveringPhyId < numOfPhys, else dmUpdateAllAdjacent, dmDiscoveringExpanderRemove and dmDownStreamDiscovering; if the status is no longer DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM it only returns.

name: dmDownStreamDiscover2ExpanderPhy
prose: Handles one SAS2 DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during downstream discovery; returns void. Behavior: returns at once with no change if dmDiscoverCheck returns agTRUE. If the response's phy id differs from discoveringPhyId it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns, without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError. Otherwise it stores the routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId] and sets discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE (both before the direct-routing check). With an attached device: direct routing to an attached edge or fanout expander records the SAS address and phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns. Otherwise, when the attached SAS address differs from the port's local address, it looks up the device with dmPortSASDeviceFind; if not found it computes the connection rate as the minimum of the port link rate and the reported logical rate and adds the device with dmPortSASDeviceAdd (STP type for STP target or SATA, otherwise SAS type; in non-full-start discovery it first tries dmFindRegNValid), and if a device results sets its dmExpander to oneExpander. A phy with no attached device or one attached to the local address adds nothing and sets no failure. name: dmSMPCompleted
prose: SMP completion callback for the discovery manager; returns void. It reads the dmSMPRequestBody from agIORequest->osData and works on the request's device and port contexts. Otherwise it decrements onePortContext->discovery.pendingSMP; if the request's port context differs from the old one it stops the discovery SMP timers for discovery-type SMP functions (report general, discover, report phy sata, configure routing), calls dmCleanAllExp on the old context, frees the bodies and returns; if the port is invalid, discovery completed or aborted it stops timers, frees the bodies, may clean up expanders when pendingSMP is 0, and returns. For a live port it stops the SMP timers, and then dispatches on whether the expander is SAS 1.1 or SAS2 (oneExpander->SAS2) and on agIOStatus. OSSA_IO_SUCCESS: for report general, discover, report phy sata, configure routing and phy control, a response length mismatch calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE), frees the bodies and returns, otherwise the matching per-function handler (dmReportGeneralRespRcvd or dmReportGeneral2RespRcvd, dmDiscoverRespRcvd or dmDiscover2RespRcvd, dmReportPhySata2Rcvd, dmConfigRoutingInfo(2)RespRcvd, dmPhyControl(2)RespRcvd) is called and the function breaks to the common tail; SMP functions the switch does not list do nothing. OSSA_IO_ABORTED and OSSA_IO_INVALID_LENGTH only log. OSSA_IO_ERROR_INTERNAL_SMP_RESOURCE resubmits with saSMPStart: on AGSA_RC_SUCCESS it increments pendingSMP, re-arms the discovery timer for discovery functions and returns without freeing; on AGSA_RC_BUSY a discovery function starts dmSMPBusyTimer and SMP_PHY_CONTROL calls dmPhyControlFailureRespRcvd; on failure a discovery function calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and SMP_PHY_CONTROL calls dmPhyControlFailureRespRcvd. In the SAS2 branch OSSA_IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_ZONE_VIOLATION calls dmHandleZoneViolation. Other statuses: for the IT-nexus-loss and non-operational statuses the device is set operational with saSetDeviceState; for a connection-rate-unsupported error with dmAllShared->RateAdjust it lowers the rate via saSetDeviceInfo or, at 1.5G, reports discovery or phy-control failure; otherwise it retries with saSMPStart while retries < SMP_RETRIES (on success or busy it increments pendingSMP and retries, starts a timer and returns), and once retries are used up it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) for discovery functions (and for phy control only with the clear-affiliation operation). name: siHDAMode
prose: Forces the SPC controller into HDA mode and loads firmware images through the boot ROM; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE. Parameters: agRoot, HDAMode (when it is 0 the function first calls siSpcSoftReset and reads the HDA status, returning AGSA_RC_FAILURE if the status is not BOOTTLOADERHDA_IDLE), userFwImg. It returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE at once if userFwImg is NULL; with SA_EXCLUDE_FW_IMG defined it also returns failure if any of the aap1, ila, iop or istr image pointers or lengths is missing. Image pointers taken from userFwImg are used as given when both the pointer and length are non-zero. The function then polls the boot ROM, copies the ISTR image (siBar4Cpy), the ILA image, the AAP1 image and the IOP image in that sequence, polling each step; any failed siBar4Cpy returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE, an HDAR_BAD_IMG or HDAR_BAD_CMD response returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE, and a poll timeout returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE except that two of the polls first jump to the label TryAfterReset when the HDA reset has not been done yet (the code at 1532-1538 and 1653-1659). It returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS only after all four image copies and polls complete and mpiWaitForConfigTable(agRoot, &mainCfg) does not return AGSA_RC_FAILURE; a failure there returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE.

name: siBar4Cpy
prose: Copies array_size bytes from parray to controller memory at offset via the BAR4 window in 64 KB pieces; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE. The window shift address is (GSMSM_AXI_LOWERADDR+offset) & SHIFT_MASK and the first piece starts at offset & OFFSET_MASK inside the window. The loop is a do-while, so even for array_size 0 it shifts BAR4 once and calls siPciMemCpy with zero dwords. Each iteration calls siBar4Shift for the current window and returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE immediately if that fails (earlier pieces stay copied and later ones are not copied). It then copies cpy_size bytes (the rest of the 64 KB window, or all remaining bytes if they fit) through siPciMemCpy as CEILING(cpy_size,4) little-endian dwords written to PCIBAR2, so up to 3 bytes beyond the end of the last piece may be read from parray and written to the card; it then advances to the next 64 KB window. After the loop it shifts BAR4 back to 0 and returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE if that final siBar4Shift fails (all bytes were already copied then), otherwise AGSA_RC_SUCCESS.

name: siHDAMode_V
prose: Loads firmware into an SPCv controller via the HDA boot-ROM DMA protocol; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE (returnVal starts as AGSA_RC_FAILURE). Precondition: agRoot->sdkData points to a valid agsaLLRoot_t whose memoryAllocated.agMemory array holds memoryAllocated.count entries. Behavior: it calls siScratchDump(agRoot) first, then returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE if userFwImg is NULL (before reading the HDA response register). It reads the HDA response status register and finds the largest allocated memory chunk (biggest), whose DMA address it uses as the transfer buffer; if aap1Len, ilaLen or iopLen exceeds biggest it returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE. Then for each enabled step (HDA_STEP_2 to HDA_STEP_8 are all defined as 1) it zeroes the buffer, copies the ILA, AAP1 or IOP image into it only when that image's length is less than biggest (an image whose length equals biggest is not copied, but the command is still issued with that length), issues the HDA DMA command or scratchpad request and polls for completion; a timeout in the ILA, AAP1 or IOP polls returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE or jumps to fw_err (which also returns the failure value); a step-5 response other than SPC_V_HDAR_EXEC jumps to bootrom_err, which returns returnVal (AGSA_RC_FAILURE at that point). Only step 8 sets returnVal to AGSA_RC_SUCCESS; there a timeout of the IOP0 state poll sets it back to AGSA_RC_FAILURE, an ILA or RAAE poll timeout is only logged, and a scratchpad-1 error state afterwards sets AGSA_RC_FAILURE and goes to fw_err. It returns returnVal at the end. It takes no locks and the caller keeps ownership of the images.

prose: Loads firmware into an SPCv controller via the HDA boot-ROM DMA protocol; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE (returnVal starts as AGSA_RC_FAILURE). name: ossaSATAEvent
prose: SATA event callback of the SM layer; returns void and uses the global gsmRoot (smIntRoot and smAllShared are derived from it with no NULL check). On OSSA_IO_XFER_ERROR_ABORTED_NCQ_MODE it scans smAllShared->MainDeviceList for the device whose agDevHandle equals agDevHandle: it returns if a list entry object is NULL, if no device matches, or if the matching device's valid flag is agFALSE. If the device's satDriveState is SAT_DEV_STATE_NORMAL it sets it to SAT_DEV_STATE_IN_RECOVERY and allocates an internal IO resource for READ LOG EXT page 10h; if allocation fails it sets satAbortAfterReset to agTRUE and returns; otherwise it fills the internal IO context and calls smsatSendReadLogExt, and if that does not return SM_RC_SUCCESS it frees the internal IO resource, sets satAbortAfterReset to agTRUE and returns; on success the recovery continues in the READ LOG EXT completion. If the drive is already not in the NORMAL state it only logs. On OSSA_IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_STP_RESOURCES_BUSY it takes the smIORequestBody from agIORequest->osData and returns if it, its smDevHandle or the device data is NULL; then, only if smAllShared->FCA is set, it does one SMP hard reset through smPhyControlSend when oneDeviceData->SMNumOfFCA is not positive (incrementing SMNumOfFCA) and otherwise only logs; with FCA clear it does nothing. All other events listed (command frame issued, PIO setup error, IT-nexus-loss variants, DEK key tag mismatch, NAK received, DMA activate timeout) and unknown events only log. It returns no value.

name: smsatTestUnitReadyCB
prose: Completion callback for the internal ATA command (SAT_GET_MEDIA_STATUS or SAT_CHECK_POWER_MODE) that implements SCSI TEST UNIT READY; returns void. It marks the internal request ioCompleted and not ioStarted and finds the original request through satIntIo. If agIOStatus is OSSA_IO_ABORTED it completes the original request with tdsmIOCompletedCB(smIOFailed, smDetailAborted), decrements the pending IO count (smsatDecrementPendingIO), frees the internal IO resource and returns. If agFirstDword is NULL and the status is not success it sets NOT_READY sense, completes the original with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION, decrements pending IO, frees the internal resource and returns. If the status is otherwise not success, a failure FIS is examined; an aborted status goes through smsatProcessAbort (not tdsmIOCompletedCB), and then per command: SAT_GET_MEDIA_STATUS sets NOT_READY sense (medium-not-present when the NM bit of the ATA error register is set), SAT_CHECK_POWER_MODE sets NOT_READY with logical-unit-does-not-respond, and any other command sets NOT_READY; each case completes the original with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION via tdsmIOCompletedCB, decrements pending IO and frees the internal resource. On success: SAT_GET_MEDIA_STATUS decrements pending IO and frees the internal resource, allocates a new internal IO and issues smsatTestUnitReady_1 (SAT_CHECK_POWER_MODE); if the allocation fails (nothing new to free) it completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION and returns; if smsatTestUnitReady_1 does not return SM_RC_SUCCESS it frees the new internal IO and completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION; if it succeeds no completion is made here and the original stays pending for the next callback. SAT_CHECK_POWER_MODE success decrements pending IO, frees the internal resource and completes the original with SCSI_STAT_GOOD and no sense. Any other command on the success path completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION, decrements pending IO and frees the resource.

name: smsatStartStopUnitCB
prose: Completion callback for the internal ATA command issued as part of SCSI START STOP UNIT (flush cache, standby, read verify sectors or media eject); returns void. It locates the original request through satIntIo (returning at 3395 on one early path) and then, if agFirstDword is NULL and the status is not success, sets ABORTED COMMAND sense (a deferred sense when the CDB IMMED bit is set, otherwise normal sense), completes the original with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION and returns. For other non-success statuses it examines the failure FIS; an aborted status is handled separately (3500-3513) and returns; otherwise a per-command error switch (flush cache, standby, read verify sectors, media eject: ABORTED COMMAND sense, deferred when IMMED is set; default: NO_SENSE sense, not deferred and independent of IMMED) completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION, then returns. On success the command switch is: SAT_FLUSH_CACHE or SAT_FLUSH_CACHE_EXT decrements pending IO, frees satIntIo, allocates a new internal IO and sends a follow-up standby via smsatStartStopUnit_1; if allocation fails or the send does not return SM_RC_SUCCESS it sets ABORTED COMMAND sense (deferred when IMMED is set), completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION and returns (freeing the new IO when it was allocated and the send failed); if the send succeeds the original stays pending for the follow-up. SAT_STANDBY decrements pending IO, frees satIntIo, completes the original with SCSI_STAT_GOOD only when the IMMED bit is clear, and sets satStopState to agTRUE. SAT_READ_VERIFY_SECTORS(_EXT) does the same completion rule and sets satStopState to agFALSE. SAT_MEDIA_EJECT decrements pending IO, frees satIntIo and completes with GOOD only when IMMED is clear. Any other command sets NO_SENSE sense, completes with CHECK_CONDITION, decrements pending IO and frees satIntIo.

name: tiCOMMgntIOCTL
prose: Management IOCTL dispatcher of the TISA layer; returns a bit32 status (IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS, IOCTL_CALL_PENDING, IOCTL_CALL_FAIL, IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE, IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_DEVICE or a handler's status) and also writes agIOCTLPayload->Status and Length. status starts as IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE; if agIOCTLPayload->Signature is not PMC_IOCTL_SIGNATURE it returns IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE at once. Otherwise it switches on MajorFunction. Cases visible in the range read: IOCTL_MJ_INI_DRIVER_IDENTIFY returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS; IOCTL_MJ_GET_DEVICE_LUN returns IOCTL_CALL_PENDING when its handler returned success, otherwise the handler's value; IOCTL_MJ_GET_EVENT_LOG1/2 with IOCTL_MN_FW_GET_TRACE_BUFFER: when the log length is not greater than the offset it sets Status IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NO_MORE_DATA (IOCTL_ERR_FW_EVENTLOG_DISABLED when the event log option is 0), Length 0 and returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS immediately, otherwise it sets ReadLength = MIN(remaining, requested), Status OK and returns success; IOCTL_MJ_FW_INFO and IOCTL_MJ_GET_FW_REV with a requested length of 0 set NO_MORE_DATA and return success, else Status OK and success; IOCTL_MJ_GET_CORE_DUMP on non-SPC sets Status IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED and success; IOCTL_MJ_GPIO returns IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_DEVICE for vendor id 0x9005, and otherwise IOCTL_CALL_PENDING when the setup succeeded or the setup's status when it did not; IOCTL_MJ_PHY_DETAILS fills the PhyDetails array and returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS; IOCTL_MJ_PHY_GENERAL_STATUS returns IOCTL_CALL_FAIL when Length is smaller than agsaPhyGeneralState_t or when tdsaGetPhyGeneralStatusIoctl returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE, sets Status NOT_SUPPORTED and returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS when it returns IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED, else IOCTL_CALL_PENDING; IOCTL_MJ_LL_TRACING: reset-index and buffer-info set Status OK and return IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS, IOCTL_MN_LL_GET_TRACE_BUFFER leaves the case without setting Status or status when the low fence or high fence check fails (status then keeps its current value, normally IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE) and otherwise sets Status OK and success; IOCTL_MJ_PORT_START and IOCTL_MJ_PORT_STOP call tiCOMPortStart or tiCOMPortStop, set Status OK or IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR and return IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS; IOCTL_MJ_GET_DRIVER_VERSION sets Status OK and returns success. The default case sets Status to IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED and returns the unchanged status, IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE. The remaining major functions delegate to per-function handlers whose results become the return value.

name: smHandleDirect
prose: Handles the identify data of a directly attached SATA device; returns void. Precondition: tiRoot, agRoot, oneDeviceData and IDdata (agsaSATAIdentifyData_t) are valid. It saves oneDeviceData->phyID, then walks tdsaAllShared->MainDeviceList; if an entry converts to a NULL device it returns immediately with nothing changed. If such an existing record is found it sets that record's valid and valid2 to agTRUE, sets its agRoot to the agRoot parameter, takes over oneDeviceData's agDevHandle (setting agDevHandle->osData to the existing record), tdPortContext and phyID, calls saDeregisterDeviceHandle(agRoot, ...) on oneDeviceData->agDevHandle unconditionally, calls saRegisterNewDevice for the existing record only if its registered flag is agFALSE, fills oneDeviceData's stored identify data with 0xFF and moves oneDeviceData from MainDeviceList to tdsaAllShared->FreeDeviceList. If no record matches, oneDeviceData's identify data is set to a copy of *IDdata. In both cases it then calls ostiPortEvent(tiPortLinkUp, tiSuccess) on tdsaAllShared->Ports[PhyID].tiPortalContext, plus a tiPortDiscoveryReady event when INITIATOR_DRIVER is defined, and returns.

name: tdsmIDCompletedCB
prose: Completion callback for the SATA identify-device request; returns void. It takes the tdIORequestBody from smIORequest->tdData and the device from smDeviceHandle. If smDeviceHandle is NULL it frees the request memory and returns without touching IDPending. Otherwise it clears oneDeviceData->satDevData.IDPending and kills the ID timer if it is running. It then returns after freeing the request memory (and for some paths reporting the device removed) in these early cases: NULL port context (frees only, no removal report); pid in the request differing from the port context id, and NULL portal context (both report removal directly or via smReportRemoval then free); NULL agRoot (frees only). For smIOSuccess it sets IDDeviceValid to agTRUE and, for a directly attached device, calls smHandleDirect and copies serial number, firmware version and model into onePortContext->remoteName, while for an expander-attached device it signals tiDeviceArrival through ostiInitiatorEvent when the port discovery state is ITD_DSTATE_COMPLETED; the request memory is then freed. For smIORetry: if the device is no longer valid, registered and attached to a port context it frees the request and sets IDDeviceValid to agFALSE; otherwise while reTries <= SM_RETRIES it restarts smIDStart: on failure it frees the request and calls smReportRemoval, on success it increments reTries, sets IDPending to agTRUE and re-arms the ID timer, keeping the request; when retries are exhausted it frees the request, clears IDDeviceValid and calls smReportRemoval. For smIOSTPResourceBusy it frees the request, clears IDDeviceValid, and when FCA is set and SMNumOfFCA is not positive increments SMNumOfFCA and sends an SMP hard reset, when FCA is set otherwise calls smReportRemoval, and when FCA is not set takes the remaining else branch (not checked beyond its control flow). For any other status it frees the request and returns if the device is not valid and registered; otherwise when tdsaAllShared->IDRetry is set and reTries <= SM_RETRIES it restarts smIDStart (failure: free, clear IDDeviceValid, report removal; success: reTries++, IDPending true, request retained), else it frees the request, clears IDDeviceValid, and either sends a hard reset (saLocalPhyControl for directly attached, tdsaPhyControlSend otherwise) once while SMNumOfID <= 0 or reports removal.

name: itdssSMPCompleted
prose: SMP completion callback for the initiator discovery code (the TD_DISCOVER build; a second definition at 2044 for builds without TD_DISCOVER is a separate stub). Returns void. It takes the request body from agIORequest->osData, its device and port context, and decodes the SMP function of the original request (from the payload with DIRECT_SMP, else by reading the request header). If the device's port context is NULL, or the request's remembered old port context is NULL, it frees the request body (and, without DIRECT_SMP, the indirect request and response buffers) and returns. Otherwise it decrements onePortContext->discovery.pendingSMP; if the port context changed, or the port is no longer valid, it kills the discovery SMP timers for discovery functions, may clean up expanders, frees the bodies and returns. For a live port it stops the timers and dispatches on agIOStatus. OSSA_IO_SUCCESS: for report general, discover, report phy sata, configure routing, phy control and report manufacturer information, a response-length mismatch calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone or tdsaSATADiscoverDone(tiError), frees the bodies and returns; otherwise the matching handler (tdsaReportGeneralRespRcvd, tdsaDiscoverRespRcvd, tdsaConfigRoutingInfoRespRcvd, tdsaPhyControlRespRcvd, tdsaReportManInfoRespRcvd, SATA report) runs and the function falls through to the common tail; unlisted SMP functions do nothing. OSSA_IO_ABORTED and OSSA_IO_INVALID_LENGTH only log. OSSA_IO_ERROR_INTERNAL_SMP_RESOURCE resubmits with saSMPStart: success (pendingSMP++, timer for discovery functions) returns without freeing; busy starts tdsaSMPBusyTimer for discovery functions or calls tdsaPhyControlFailureRespRcvd for phy control; failure calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) for discovery functions or tdsaPhyControlFailureRespRcvd for phy control. Other statuses: while retries < SMP_RETRIES it marks the device operational for the nexus-loss statuses and calls saSMPStart again, increments pendingSMP and retries and returns without freeing; once retries are used up it handles non-operational and in-recovery states and reports discovery failure (tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError)) for discovery functions, and for phy control handles the clear-affiliation and hard-reset operations. All other paths reach the tail that frees the request body and, without DIRECT_SMP, the indirect buffers, then returns.

name: tdssReportRemovals
prose: Reports device removals for a port after a port event; returns void. Precondition: onePortContext->eventPhyID indexes tdsaAllShared->eventSource (the code reads eventSource[PhyID].EventValid before it tests PhyID != 0xFF). Behavior: if eventSource[PhyID].EventValid is agTRUE, onePortContext->RegisteredDevNums is 0 and PhyID is not 0xFF, it acknowledges the hardware event with saHwEventAck (only logging a non-success result) and clears EventValid; then if onePortContext->valid is agFALSE it moves every MainDeviceList device of this port to FreeDeviceList (filling its identify data with 0xFF, under TD_DEVICE_LOCK), reinitializes the port context with tdsaPortContextReInit and moves it from the main list to FreePortContextList under TD_PORT_LOCK; if valid is agTRUE (still inside that outer condition) it returns immediately if MainDeviceList is empty, and otherwise recycles those devices of this port that have valid, valid2 and registered all agFALSE into FreeDeviceList. When the outer condition is false none of that is done. After that, in all cases that did not return, it returns immediately if MainDeviceList is empty and otherwise visits every device of this port: for registered devices that are SSP, STP, SATA or SMP targets it calls tdsaAbortAll, for other registered devices it calls saDeregisterDeviceHandle, then it sets valid, valid2 and registered to agFALSE and NumOfFCA to 0 for every device of the port and, when flag is agTRUE, sets tdPortContext to agNULL; it records a removal when a device that was valid and registered is an SSP target, STP target or SATA device, and finally issues one ostiInitiatorEvent(tiIntrEventTypeDeviceChange, tiDeviceRemoval) for the port if any such removal was recorded. A NULL device object in the list returns immediately. TD_DEVICE_LOCK and TD_PORT_LOCK are released in each place they are taken.

name: tdsaSASUpStreamDiscoverExpanderPhy
prose: Handles one SMP DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during upstream discovery; returns void. If onePortContext->valid is agFALSE it calls tdsaSASDiscoverAbort and returns. If pDiscoverResp->phyIdentifier differs from discoveringPhyId it calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) and returns, recording no error address. Otherwise it stores the response's routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId]. If the expander's device is a fanout expander and the routing is subtractive it records the device's SAS address and phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) and returns; for a fanout expander with other routing nothing more happens in this step. For a non-fanout expander with an attached device and subtractive routing only: it adds the upstream phy (tdsaSASExpanderUpStreamPhyAdd); if hasUpStreamDevice was already set and the upstream address differs from the attached address it records the error address and calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError); otherwise it sets hasUpStreamDevice and the upstream address, and when the attached address differs from the port's local address it looks the device up with tdsaPortSASDeviceFind: found as an edge expander gives either oneExpander->tdUpStreamExpander = that expander (upstream addresses consistent) or error-address recording plus tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError); not found, it adds the device with tdsaPortSASDeviceAdd (STP type for STP target or SATA, otherwise SAS; in non-full-start discovery first looking for a registered valid one), and if that produced a device it allocates and queues an expander for an attached edge or fanout expander (setting tdUpStreamExpander, or tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) on allocation failure with no error address) or for an end device sets its expander link and clears tdUpStreamExpander, and if no device was produced it calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) with no error address. An edge expander with an attached device but non-subtractive routing, or with no attached device, only has its routing attribute stored. All paths that do not return early then increment discoveringPhyId; if discovery.status is DISCOVERY_UP_STREAM it either sends the next phy (tdsaDiscoverSend) or finishes the expander (adjacent update, tdssSASDiscoveringExpanderRemove, tdsaSASUpStreamDiscovering).

Otherwise it stores the routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId] and sets discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE. With an attached device: direct routing to an attached expander records the error address and phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) and returns; otherwise, if the attached SAS address differs from the port's local address and the device is not yet known, subtractive routing to an attached expander records the error address and calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError), and otherwise the device is added (STP or SAS type; in non-full-start discovery a registered valid one is reused first); for an added device, table routing to a fanout expander records the error address and calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError), table routing to an edge expander allocates an expander and, if oneExpander->configRouteTable is set, sets up routing, with an allocation failure calling tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) without an error address; a failed device add also calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) without an error address. Every path that did not return early then increments discoveringPhyId; if the status is still DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM it sends the next phy (tdsaDiscoverSend) when phys remain, otherwise it removes the expander from the discovering list and continues downstream discovery.
